summary: Feature release after 5.38.0. Meetings get mandatory join links, licensed join-by-link, calendar-managed meetings and emails sent by brig; custom backends, login budgets, DPoP nonces and connections can move to PostgreSQL; federated contact status, mock TOTP endpoints and fixes for MLS and SCIM-managed accounts are included, and the ldap-scim-bridge chart is no longer published from wire-server. Before deploying: if galley.config.postgresMigration.conversationCodes is still cassandra, move it to migration-to-postgresql, or meetings fail with 500 link-unavailable; then set license and brig emailSMS if you use meeting join links or meeting emails.

changes.description: Every meeting now has a join link backed by a live join code, and meeting join codes are only stored in PostgreSQL. With galley.config.postgresMigration.conversationCodes on cassandra (the chart default), creating a meeting or refreshing its link fails with 500 link-unavailable, and so do reads of meetings that have no live join code, on every API version. Before upgrading, set conversationCodes to migration-to-postgresql (dual-write, guest links stay on Cassandra) or postgresql, and keep a join-link URI configured (galley settings.conversationCodeURI, or the domain of the user in settings.multiIngress).

From client API version 19 every meeting carries its join link: a one-off data migration gives each existing meeting without a live join code a canonical one, without rotating existing codes, and replaces the periodic galley backfill. Refreshing a meeting link reports has_password according to the password supplied with the refresh.

Joining a meeting by link is licensed: POST /meeting/{domain}/{key}/{code}/join and GET /meeting/{domain}/{key}/{code}/code-check return 403 id-feature-error unless the deployment licence covers invitation links. Set the new top-level Helm value license to a licence payload (schema_version 1) that covers invitation links before upgrading if you use join links.
Client API version 19 is final and supported; version 20 is now the development version.

GET /license (client API version 19, authenticated) returns the meetings licensing flags of the deployment: invitation_links, emails_sending and calendars_integration, all false when the deployment has no valid licence.

Meeting invitation, update and cancellation emails are now rendered and sent by brig, and sent when a meeting is created, edited, has its link refreshed or is deleted. Sender, transport and branding come from brig's emailSMS configuration; the keys under galley.config.settings.meetings.email (from, useSES, aws, smtp, templateDir, branding) and galley.secrets.smtpPassword are no longer read. The presence of the legacy galley block still enables meeting emails and its replyTo feeds brig's emailSMS.general.meeting.replyTo. Emails are only sent when galley.config.settings.meetings.emailsEnabled is true (or the legacy block is present) and the deployment licence covers meeting emails. Before upgrading, check brig's emailSMS sender and transport if you send meeting emails.
Meeting invitation, update and cancellation emails attach an RFC 5545 .ics calendar file, and the Add to calendar link references the attachment.

Calendar-managed meetings (client API version 19): POST /meetings takes an optional externally_managed_by with externally_calendar_event_id and externally_calendar_id. Only access tokens issued to an OAuth client listed in galley.config.settings.meetings.calendarOAuthClients can create or change them (Wire clients get 403 externally-managed-by-calendar, other callers and inconsistent pairings 400 invalid-op, an unlicensed create 403 id-feature-error), and they send no emails through Wire. Access tokens carry the OAuth client id; nginz forwards it to the services as Z-OAuth-Client and strips any value sent by a caller. Upgrade nginz before setting calendarOAuthClients, and refresh OAuth access tokens issued before this release, which carry no client id. Nothing changes until calendarOAuthClients is set.

Meeting join links admit temporary guests: meeting conversations store a guest access role, existing meetings are updated by a data migration, and access updates on a meeting conversation are rejected with 403 invalid-op because the meetings subsystem owns their access roles.
Participants removed from a meeting receive a meeting.delete event, so their clients drop the meeting as soon as they are excluded from the meeting conversation.

PostgreSQL storage for custom backends, login budgets, DPoP nonces and connections, opt-in through the new galley.config.postgresMigration keys customBackend, budget, nonce and connections (cassandra by default). Custom backends, nonces and connections are backfilled by background-worker (migrateCustomBackend, migrateNonce, migrateConnections); budgets have no backfill, so keep budget on migration-to-postgresql for at least the longest limitFailedLogins.timeout before switching to postgresql. Follow the migration pattern of the configuration options documentation.

PUT /teams/{tid}/members/{uid}/verification-email lets a team admin resend the verification email of a member whose email address is still unverified: 202 when an email is sent, 204 when there is nothing to verify.

Mock endpoints for TOTP (RFC 6238) second factors from client API version 19: POST /self/totp, POST /self/totp/{id}/activate, GET /self/totp, PUT /self/totp/{id} and DELETE /self/totp/{id}. They parse the request and return generated data; nothing is stored and no code is checked. nginz routes them without OAuth scopes.

Seventeen endpoints accept an optional totp_code field in their request body, prefixed totp:123456 for an authenticator code or recovery:xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx for a recovery code, among them POST /login, DELETE /self, PUT /self/password, POST /clients, DELETE /teams/{tid} and POST /auth-tokens. The field is validated for format only: no second factor is checked yet and existing authentication requirements are unchanged.
Team feature mfa-totp, disabled and locked by default (galley settings.featureFlags). It exists so that clients can test their interface against the TOTP mock endpoints; it enforces nothing.

Federation error responses include federation_domain, the requested peer, and, when an SRV target is known, srv_target and srv_target_domain. The domain and path fields are unchanged. Federation error logs carry the same information.
nginx-ingress-services: the federator ingress only exposes paths under /federation instead of every path of the federator.

contact_status in POST /list-users?include-contact-status=true covers federated users. The requester's backend sends its context (MLS availability, allowed cipher suites) in one batched call per remote domain, through the new get-users-contact-status call of the brig federation API (development version 5); the remote backend rejects more than 1000 users with HTTP 400. Requests to backends on a federation version below 5 log an error at level Warn until that backend is upgraded.
Gundeck exports new Prometheus metrics on stored pushes (wire_push_stored_*), notification fetches (wire_notification_fetch*) and websocket deliveries (wire_push_ws_delivered_presences*).

backoffice: the ports of the galeb and ibis services are configurable with backoffice.config.galebPort and backoffice.config.ibisPort. Both default to 8080, the value that was hard-coded, so nothing changes unless you set them.

nginz gets a /log-traces route to a new log-analyzer upstream (10 MB body limit, rate-limited per address). log-analyzer is in nginx_conf.ignored_upstreams by default, so the route only exists once you remove it from that list and run a log-analyzer service.
Validating the key-package uploads of a client loads its MLS public key at most once per signature scheme per request instead of repeating the lookup.

The ldap-scim-bridge Helm chart is no longer published from wire-server. It lives in wireapp/ldap-scim-bridge and is released there with its own version (6.0.0 onwards) at oci://quay.io/wire/charts/stable/ldap-scim-bridge. The 5.x charts already published stay available, and the openldap test chart moved to examples/openldap in that repository. If you deploy ldap-scim-bridge, take the chart from its new location.
Re-joining an MLS group with an external commit could drop the client from the member list kept by the backend, silently stopping message delivery to that client.
MLS timestamp mismatches that broke reply quotes. The fix applies only when both backends enable federation API version 5, the development version, which the chart disables by default.
Legacy Proteus team 1:1 conversations are no longer migrated in place as MLS groups, which could split messages between the migrated group and the canonical MLS 1:1 conversation.
Legacy team 1:1 conversations are excluded from the prevention of admin-less groups.

Changing the permissions of a team collaborator no longer removes them from conversations, and collaborators are removed from MLS 1:1 conversations with team members when the collaboration ends, unless the two users can still reach each other another way.

SCIM-managed accounts are protected: team admins cannot change the team role of a SCIM-managed user and users cannot delete their SCIM-managed email address. SCIM role reads and updates for pending invitations are fixed and the assigned role is kept when the invitation is accepted.

migrations.description: If galley.config.postgresMigration.conversationCodes is cassandra, set it to migration-to-postgresql (or postgresql once the conversation codes are migrated) and check that settings.conversationCodeURI or settings.multiIngress is set in galley.
If you use meeting join links, set the top-level Helm value license to a licence payload that covers invitation links; without it the join and code-check endpoints return 403 id-feature-error.

If you send meeting emails, configure the sender, transport and branding in brig's emailSMS (they are no longer read from galley.config.settings.meetings.email), set galley.config.settings.meetings.emailsEnabled to true, optionally brig.config.emailSMS.general.meeting.replyTo, and make sure the licence covers meeting emails.

To enable calendar-managed meetings, upgrade nginz first, then set galley.config.settings.meetings.calendarOAuthClients to the OAuth client ids of the calendar integration, and have the integration refresh its access tokens.
SQL migration 20261019090000-meeting-join-code-backfill gives every meeting without a live join code a canonical one. It runs once per database at service startup and never rotates an existing code.
migrations.order: at startup, before meetings are served

migrations.description: SQL migration 20261102120000-meetings-conversation-guest-role stores the guest access role of the conversations of existing meetings, so that temporary guests can still join through existing links.
SQL migration 20261015120000-meetings-externally-managed-by adds three nullable columns to the meetings table for calendar-managed meetings.
SQL migrations create the PostgreSQL tables of the budget, connections, custom backend and nonce stores. They stay unused while the matching postgresMigration keys are cassandra.

configuration.description: The default is unchanged, but meetings now need meeting join codes in PostgreSQL: set migration-to-postgresql or postgresql, otherwise meetings fail with 500 link-unavailable.
Storage of custom backends: cassandra, migration-to-postgresql or postgresql. Mandatory in the brig, galley and background-worker configuration; the chart renders the default.
Storage of login budgets (rate-limit counters). No backfill: stay on migration-to-postgresql for at least the longest limitFailedLogins.timeout before switching to postgresql.
Storage of DPoP replay nonces: cassandra, migration-to-postgresql or postgresql.
Storage of user connections: cassandra, migration-to-postgresql or postgresql.
Starts the backfill of custom backends to PostgreSQL. Set postgresMigration.customBackend to migration-to-postgresql first.
Starts the backfill of DPoP nonces to PostgreSQL. Set postgresMigration.nonce to migration-to-postgresql first.
Starts the backfill of connections to PostgreSQL. Set postgresMigration.connections to migration-to-postgresql first.

Optional licence payload (base64url, produced by the wire-licensing CLI), applied deployment-wide: rendered into galley's settings.license and background-worker's license. Empty means an unlicensed deployment: meeting join-by-link returns 403 id-feature-error and meeting emails are not sent.
When true, galley asks brig to send meeting emails; rendering and transport are brig's. The presence of the legacy galley.config.settings.meetings.email block also enables them.
Optional Reply-To address of meeting emails. Falls back to galley.config.settings.meetings.email.replyTo when that legacy block is present.
Deprecated. Its presence still enables meeting emails and its replyTo feeds brig's emailSMS.general.meeting.replyTo; from, useSES, aws, smtp, templateDir and branding are ignored.
No longer read by galley: meeting emails use brig's SMTP or SES configuration.

OAuth client ids (as returned by brig's POST /i/oauth/clients) of the calendar integration. Only access tokens issued to these clients can create and change calendar-managed meetings. Empty: nobody can. Upgrade nginz before setting it.
Defaults of the mfa-totp team feature (status, lock status, require_for_all_members, compulsory_for_owners_and_admins). It only supports interface testing against the TOTP mock endpoints.
Port of the galeb service that backoffice calls. Same value as the one that was hard-coded.
Port of the ibis service that backoffice calls. Same value as the one that was hard-coded.
The list now contains log-analyzer (it was empty). If you override it, for example to add cannon, keep log-analyzer in it unless you run that service.
